title: Air Pollution
content:
# Air Pollution

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Identify the main air pollutants and their sources
- Explain the problems caused by each pollutant
- Describe how catalytic converters reduce pollution
- Discuss methods to reduce air pollution

## Introduction

**Air pollution** refers to harmful substances released into the atmosphere that can damage health, ecosystems, and buildings. Most air pollution comes from burning fossil fuels, but industrial processes and agriculture also contribute.

## Key Concepts

### Main Air Pollutants

| Pollutant | Formula | Main sources |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| Carbon monoxide | CO | Incomplete combustion |
| Nitrogen oxides | NOₓ | High temperature combustion |
| Sulfur dioxide | SO₂ | Burning fossil fuels containing sulfur |
| Particulates | PM | Combustion, industry |
| Unburned hydrocarbons | CₓHᵧ | Incomplete combustion |
| Ozone (ground level) | O₃ | Secondary pollutant |

### Carbon Monoxide (CO)

**Source:**
- Incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels
- Occurs when oxygen supply is limited

**Formation:**
$$2\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}$$ (limited oxygen)

Compare with complete combustion:
$$\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2$$ (excess oxygen)

**Problems:**
| Problem | Explanation |
|---------|-------------|
| Toxic to humans | Binds to haemoglobin in blood |
| Reduces oxygen transport | Haemoglobin can't carry oxygen |
| Colourless and odourless | Hard to detect |
| Can cause death | In enclosed spaces |

**Reducing CO emissions:**
- Ensure complete combustion (sufficient oxygen)
- Regular vehicle maintenance
- Catalytic converters in vehicles

### Nitrogen Oxides (NOₓ)

**Sources:**
- High temperature combustion (car engines, power stations)
- Nitrogen and oxygen from air react at high temperatures

**Formation:**
$$\text{N}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}$$

$$2\text{NO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2$$

**Problems:**
| Problem | Explanation |
|---------|-------------|
| Respiratory problems | Irritates lungs and airways |
| Acid rain | Forms nitric acid in atmosphere |
| Photochemical smog | Reacts with hydrocarbons in sunlight |
| Ground-level ozone | Contributes to ozone formation |

### Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂)

**Sources:**
- Burning fossil fuels containing sulfur
- Coal and oil contain sulfur impurities
- Volcanic emissions (natural source)

**Formation:**
$$\text{S} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_2$$

**Problems:**
| Problem | Explanation |
|---------|-------------|
| Acid rain | Forms sulfuric acid in atmosphere |
| Respiratory problems | Irritates airways |
| Damages plants | Affects leaf surfaces |
| Damages buildings | Corrodes limestone, marble |

### Particulates (PM)

**What are they?**
- Tiny solid particles or liquid droplets
- PM₁₀: particles < 10 micrometres
- PM₂.₅: particles < 2.5 micrometres (most dangerous)

**Sources:**
- Diesel engines
- Industrial processes
- Construction
- Burning wood and coal
- Dust and pollen (natural)

**Problems:**
| Problem | Explanation |
|---------|-------------|
| Respiratory diseases | Particles enter lungs |
| Heart disease | Fine particles enter bloodstream |
| Reduced visibility | Causes haze |
| Climate effects | Can affect temperature |
| Deposits on surfaces | Makes buildings dirty |

### Catalytic Converters

**What are they?**
- Devices fitted to vehicle exhausts
- Contain catalysts (platinum, palladium, rhodium)
- Convert harmful gases to less harmful ones

**Reactions in a catalytic converter:**

1. **Oxidation of CO:**
$$2\text{CO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2$$

2. **Oxidation of hydrocarbons:**
$$\text{C}_x\text{H}_y + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

3. **Reduction of NOₓ:**
$$2\text{NO} \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

$$2\text{CO} + 2\text{NO} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + \text{N}_2$$

**Summary of conversions:**
| Input | Output |
|-------|--------|
| CO | CO₂ |
| Unburned hydrocarbons | CO₂ + H₂O |
| NOₓ | N₂ |

### Other Methods to Reduce Air Pollution

**Power stations:**
| Method | Pollutant reduced |
|--------|------------------|
| Flue gas desulfurisation | SO₂ |
| Low NOₓ burners | NOₓ |
| Electrostatic precipitators | Particulates |
| Bag filters | Particulates |

**Transport:**
| Method | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Electric vehicles | No direct emissions |
| Better public transport | Fewer cars |
| Congestion charges | Reduces traffic |
| Low emission zones | Restricts high-polluting vehicles |
| Cycling infrastructure | Alternative to cars |

**Industry:**
| Method | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Regulations and monitoring | Enforces limits |
| Cleaner production processes | Reduces emissions |
| Filters and scrubbers | Removes pollutants |

### Flue Gas Desulfurisation

**Process:**
- Removes SO₂ from power station exhaust gases
- Uses calcium oxide (CaO) or calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂)

**Reaction with calcium oxide:**
$$\text{CaO} + \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_3$$

**Reaction with calcium hydroxide:**
$$\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Product:**
- Calcium sulfite can be oxidised to calcium sulfate (gypsum)
- Used in building materials

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** Explain how carbon monoxide is formed and why it is dangerous.

**Solution:**
**Formation:**
- Carbon monoxide is formed by incomplete combustion
- Occurs when carbon-containing fuels burn with insufficient oxygen
- Equation: 2C + O₂ → 2CO
- Common in car engines, faulty boilers, blocked chimneys

**Why it is dangerous:**
- Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells
- It binds more strongly than oxygen
- Haemoglobin cannot carry oxygen to body tissues
- This causes oxygen starvation
- Symptoms: headache, dizziness, confusion, unconsciousness
- Can be fatal in high concentrations
- Colourless and odourless, so hard to detect

---

**Example 2:** Describe how a catalytic converter reduces air pollution from vehicle exhausts.

**Solution:**
- Catalytic converters are fitted to vehicle exhausts
- They contain precious metal catalysts (platinum, palladium, rhodium)
- These catalysts speed up reactions that convert harmful gases

**Three main reactions:**
1. Carbon monoxide is oxidised to carbon dioxide:
   2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂

2. Unburned hydrocarbons are oxidised:
   CₓHᵧ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O

3. Nitrogen oxides are reduced to nitrogen:
   2NO → N₂ + O₂

**Result:**
- Harmful CO, hydrocarbons, and NOₓ are converted
- Products are less harmful (CO₂, H₂O, N₂)
- Significantly reduces vehicle emissions

---

**Example 3:** Explain how power stations can reduce sulfur dioxide emissions.

**Solution:**
**The problem:**
- Coal and oil contain sulfur impurities
- When burned, sulfur dioxide (SO₂) is produced
- SO₂ causes acid rain and respiratory problems

**Flue gas desulfurisation:**
- Exhaust gases pass through a scrubber
- Calcium oxide or calcium hydroxide is used
- SO₂ reacts with these substances:
  CaO + SO₂ → CaSO₃
  Ca(OH)₂ + SO₂ → CaSO₃ + H₂O

**The product:**
- Calcium sulfite is formed
- Can be oxidised to calcium sulfate (gypsum)
- Gypsum can be sold for building materials

**Effectiveness:**
- Removes up to 95% of SO₂
- Widely used in modern power stations

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Thinking catalytic converters remove CO₂
- **Correct:** They convert CO to CO₂ (which is less immediately harmful)

- **Mistake:** Confusing complete and incomplete combustion
- **Correct:** Complete → CO₂; Incomplete → CO

- **Mistake:** Thinking electric vehicles produce no pollution
- **Correct:** They produce no direct emissions, but electricity generation may cause pollution

## Practice Questions

1. Name three pollutants produced by burning fossil fuels. (3 marks)

2. Explain how carbon monoxide is formed and why it is toxic. (4 marks)

3. Describe the problems caused by sulfur dioxide in the atmosphere. (3 marks)

4. Explain how a catalytic converter works. Include equations. (5 marks)

5. Describe how flue gas desulfurisation reduces SO₂ emissions. (4 marks)

6. Suggest three ways air pollution from transport could be reduced. (3 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Air pollution | Harmful substances in the atmosphere |
| Incomplete combustion | Burning with insufficient oxygen, producing CO |
| Catalytic converter | Device that converts harmful exhaust gases |
| Particulates | Tiny solid or liquid particles in air |
| Flue gas desulfurisation | Process to remove SO₂ from exhaust gases |
| Photochemical smog | Pollution caused by sunlight reacting with pollutants |

## Summary

- **Main pollutants:** CO, NOₓ, SO₂, particulates, hydrocarbons
- **Carbon monoxide:** From incomplete combustion, toxic (binds to haemoglobin)
- **Nitrogen oxides:** From high-temp combustion, cause acid rain and smog
- **Sulfur dioxide:** From burning sulfur in fuels, causes acid rain
- **Particulates:** Solid particles, cause respiratory and heart problems
- **Catalytic converters:** Convert CO → CO₂, NOₓ → N₂, hydrocarbons → CO₂ + H₂O
- **Reducing pollution:** Catalytic converters, desulfurisation, electric vehicles, cleaner fuels
